1533.label: Exodus 1:1
1533.text: Now these are the names of Israel’s sons who came into Egypt with Jacob; each man and his household came:

1536.label: Exodus 1:4
1536.text: Dan and Naphʹta·li, Gad and Ashʹer.

1537.label: Exodus 1:5
1537.text: And all the souls who issued out of Jacob’s upper thigh came to be seventy souls, but Joseph was already in Egypt.

1538.label: Exodus 1:6
1538.text: Eventually Joseph died, and also all his brothers and all that generation.

1539.label: Exodus 1:7
1539.text: And the sons of Israel became fruitful and began to swarm; and they kept on multiplying and growing mightier at a very extraordinary rate, so that the land got to be filled with them.

1540.label: Exodus 1:8
1540.text: In time there arose over Egypt a new king who did not know Joseph.

1541.label: Exodus 1:9
1541.text: And he proceeded to say to his people: “Look! The people of the sons of Israel are more numerous and mightier than we are.

1542.label: Exodus 1:10
1542.text: Come on! Let us deal shrewdly with them, for fear they may multiply, and it must turn out that, in case war should befall us, then they certainly will also be added to those who hate us and will fight against us and go up out of the country.”

1543.label: Exodus 1:11
1543.text: So they set over them chiefs of forced labor for the purpose of oppressing them in their burden-bearing; and they went building cities as storage places for Pharʹaoh, namely, Piʹthom and Ra·amʹses.

1544.label: Exodus 1:12
1544.text: But the more they would oppress them, the more they would multiply and the more they kept spreading abroad, so that they felt a sickening dread as a result of the sons of Israel.

1545.label: Exodus 1:13
1545.text: Consequently the Egyptians made the sons of Israel slave under tyranny.

1546.label: Exodus 1:14
1546.text: And they kept making their life bitter with hard slavery at clay mortar and bricks and with every form of slavery in the field, yes, every form of slavery of theirs in which they used them as slaves under tyranny.

1547.label: Exodus 1:15
1547.text: Later on the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, the name of one of whom was Shiphʹrah and the name of the other Puʹah,

1548.label: Exodus 1:16
1548.text: yes, he went so far as to say: “When YOU help the Hebrew women to give birth and YOU do see them on the stool for childbirth, if it is a son, YOU must also put it to death; but if it is a daughter, it must also live.”

1549.label: Exodus 1:17
1549.text: However, the midwives feared the [true] God, and they did not do as the king of Egypt had spoken to them, but they would preserve the male children alive.

1550.label: Exodus 1:18
1550.text: In time the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them: “Why is it YOU have done this thing, in that YOU preserved the male children alive?”

1551.label: Exodus 1:19
1551.text: In turn the midwives said to Pharʹaoh: “Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women. Because they are lively, they have already given birth before the midwife can come in to them.”

1552.label: Exodus 1:20
1552.text: So God dealt well with the midwives; and the people kept growing more numerous and becoming very mighty.

1553.label: Exodus 1:21
1553.text: And it came about that because the midwives had feared the [true] God he later presented them with families.

1554.label: Exodus 1:22
1554.text: Finally Pharʹaoh commanded all his people, saying: “Every newborn son YOU are to throw into the river Nile, but every daughter YOU are to preserve alive.”

1555.label: Exodus 2:1
1555.text: Meantime, a certain man of the house of Leʹvi went ahead and took a daughter of Leʹvi.

1556.label: Exodus 2:2
1556.text: And the woman became pregnant and brought a son to birth. When she saw how good-looking he was, she kept him concealed for three lunar months.

1557.label: Exodus 2:3
1557.text: When she was no longer able to conceal him, she then took for him an ark of papyrus and coated it with bitumen and pitch and put the child in it and put it among the reeds by the bank of the river Nile.

1558.label: Exodus 2:4
1558.text: Further, his sister stationed herself at a distance to find out what would be done with him.

1559.label: Exodus 2:5
1559.text: After a while Pharʹaoh’s daughter came down to bathe in the Nile River, and her female attendants were walking by the side of the Nile River. And she caught sight of the ark in the middle of the reeds. Immediately she sent her slave girl that she might get it.

1560.label: Exodus 2:6
1560.text: When she opened it she got to see the child, and here the boy was weeping. At that she felt compassion for him, although she said: “This is one of the children of the Hebrews.”

1561.label: Exodus 2:7
1561.text: Then his sister said to Pharʹaoh’s daughter: “Shall I go and specially call for you a nursing woman from the Hebrew women that she may nurse the child for you?”

1562.label: Exodus 2:8
1562.text: So Pharʹaoh’s daughter said to her: “Go!” At once the maiden went and called the child’s mother.

1563.label: Exodus 2:9
1563.text: Pharʹaoh’s daughter then said to her: “Take this child with you and nurse him for me, and I myself shall give you your wages.” Accordingly the woman took the child and nursed him.

1564.label: Exodus 2:10
1564.text: And the child grew up. Then she brought him to Pharʹaoh’s daughter, so that he became a son to her; and she proceeded to call his name Moses and to say: “It is because I have drawn him out of the water.”

1565.label: Exodus 2:11
1565.text: Now it came about in those days, as Moses was becoming strong, that he went out to his brothers that he might look at the burdens they were bearing; and he caught sight of a certain Egyptian striking a certain Hebrew of his brothers.

1566.label: Exodus 2:12
1566.text: So he turned this way and that and saw there was nobody in sight. Then he struck the Egyptian down and hid him in the sand.

1567.label: Exodus 2:13
1567.text: However, he went out on the following day and here there were two Hebrew men struggling with each other. So he said to the one in the wrong: “Why should you strike your companion?”

1568.label: Exodus 2:14
1568.text: At this he said: “Who appointed you as a prince and judge over us? Are you intending to kill me just as you killed the Egyptian?” Moses now got afraid and said: “Surely the thing has become known!”

1569.label: Exodus 2:15
1569.text: Subsequently Pharʹaoh got to hear of this thing, and he attempted to kill Moses; but Moses ran away from Pharʹaoh that he might dwell in the land of Midʹi·an; and he took a seat by a well.

1570.label: Exodus 2:16
1570.text: Now the priest of Midʹi·an had seven daughters, and as usual they came and drew water and filled the gutters to water their father’s flock.

1571.label: Exodus 2:17
1571.text: And as usual the shepherds came and drove them away. At this Moses got up and helped the women out and watered their flock.

1572.label: Exodus 2:18
1572.text: So when they came home to Reuʹel their father he exclaimed: “How is it YOU have come home so quickly today?”

1573.label: Exodus 2:19
1573.text: To this they said: “A certain Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds and, besides, he actually drew water for us that he might water the flock.”

1574.label: Exodus 2:20
1574.text: Then he said to his daughters: “But where is he? Why is it that YOU have left the man behind? Call him, that he may eat bread.”

1575.label: Exodus 2:21
1575.text: After that Moses showed willingness to dwell with the man, and he gave Zip·poʹrah his daughter to Moses.

1576.label: Exodus 2:22
1576.text: Later she bore a son and he called his name Gerʹshom, because, he said: “An alien resident I have come to be in a foreign land.”

1577.label: Exodus 2:23
1577.text: And it came about during those many days that the king of Egypt finally died, but the sons of Israel continued to sigh because of the slavery and to cry out in complaint, and their cry for help kept going up to the [true] God because of the slavery.

1578.label: Exodus 2:24
1578.text: In time God heard their groaning and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

1579.label: Exodus 2:25
1579.text: So God looked on the sons of Israel and God took notice.

1580.label: Exodus 3:1
1580.text: And Moses became a shepherd of the flock of Jethʹro, the priest of Midʹi·an, whose son-in-law he was. While he was driving the flock to the west side of the wilderness, he came at length to the mountain of the [true] God, to Hoʹreb.

1581.label: Exodus 3:2
1581.text: Then Jehovah’s angel appeared to him in a flame of fire in the midst of a thornbush. As he kept looking, why, here the thornbush was burning with the fire and yet the thornbush was not consumed.

1582.label: Exodus 3:3
1582.text: At this Moses said: “Let me just turn aside that I may inspect this great phenomenon, as to why the thornbush is not burnt up.”

1583.label: Exodus 3:4
1583.text: When Jehovah saw that he turned aside to inspect, God at once called to him out of the midst of the thornbush and said: “Moses! Moses!” to which he said: “Here I am.”

1584.label: Exodus 3:5
1584.text: Then he said: “Do not come near here. Draw your sandals from off your feet, because the place where you are standing is holy ground.”

1585.label: Exodus 3:6
1585.text: And he went on to say: “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.” Then Moses concealed his face, because he was afraid to look at the [true] God.

1586.label: Exodus 3:7
1586.text: And Jehovah added: “Unquestionably I have seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their outcry as a result of those who drive them to work; because I well know the pains they suffer.

1587.label: Exodus 3:8
1587.text: And I am proceeding to go down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a land good and spacious, to a land flowing with milk and honey, to the locality of the Caʹnaan·ites and the Hitʹtites and the Amʹor·ites and the Perʹiz·zites and the Hiʹvites and the Jebʹu·sites.

1588.label: Exodus 3:9
1588.text: And now, look! the outcry of the sons of Israel has come to me, and I have seen also the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.

1589.label: Exodus 3:10
1589.text: And now come and let me send you to Pharʹaoh, and you bring my people the sons of Israel out of Egypt.”

1590.label: Exodus 3:11
1590.text: However, Moses said to the [true] God: “Who am I that I should go to Pharʹaoh and that I have to bring the sons of Israel out of Egypt?”

1591.label: Exodus 3:12
1591.text: To this he said: “Because I shall prove to be with you, and this is the sign for you that it is I who have sent you: After you have brought the people out of Egypt, YOU people will serve the [true] God on this mountain.”

1592.label: Exodus 3:13
1592.text: Nevertheless, Moses said to the [true] God: “Suppose I am now come to the sons of Israel and I do say to them, ‘The God of YOUR forefathers has sent me to YOU,’ and they do say to me, ‘What is his name?’ What shall I say to them?”

1593.label: Exodus 3:14
1593.text: At this God said to Moses: “I SHALL PROVE TO BE WHAT I SHALL PROVE TO BE.” And he added: “This is what you are to say to the sons of Israel, ‘I SHALL PROVE TO BE has sent me to YOU.’”

1594.label: Exodus 3:15
1594.text: Then God said once more to Moses: “This is what you are to say to the sons of Israel, ‘Jehovah the God of YOUR forefathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, has sent me to YOU.’ This is my name to time indefinite, and this is the memorial of me to generation after generation.

1595.label: Exodus 3:16
1595.text: You go, and you must gather the older men of Israel, and you must say to them, ‘Jehovah the God of YOUR forefathers has appeared to me, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying: “I will without fail give attention to YOU and to what is being done to YOU in Egypt.

1596.label: Exodus 3:17
1596.text: And so I say, I shall bring YOU up out of affliction by the Egyptians to the land of the Caʹnaan·ites and the Hitʹtites and the Amʹor·ites and the Perʹiz·zites and the Hiʹvites and the Jebʹu·sites, to a land flowing with milk and honey.”’

1597.label: Exodus 3:18
1597.text: “And they will certainly listen to your voice, and you must come, you and the older men of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and YOU men must say to him, ‘Jehovah the God of the Hebrews has come in touch with us, and now we want to go, please, a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we want to sacrifice to Jehovah our God.’

1598.label: Exodus 3:19
1598.text: And I, even I, well know that the king of Egypt will not give YOU permission to go except by a strong hand.

1599.label: Exodus 3:20
1599.text: And I shall have to stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonderful acts that I shall do in the midst of it; and after that he will send YOU out.

1600.label: Exodus 3:21
1600.text: And I will give this people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians; and it will certainly occur that when YOU go, YOU will not go empty-handed.

1601.label: Exodus 3:22
1601.text: And each woman must ask from her neighbor and from the woman residing as an alien in her house articles of silver and articles of gold and mantles, and YOU must put them upon YOUR sons and YOUR daughters; and YOU must strip the Egyptians.”

1602.label: Exodus 4:1
1602.text: However, Moses in answering said: “But suppose they do not believe me and do not listen to my voice, because they are going to say, ‘Jehovah did not appear to you.’”

1603.label: Exodus 4:2
1603.text: Then Jehovah said to him: “What is that in your hand?” to which he said: “A rod.”

1604.label: Exodus 4:3
1604.text: Next he said: “Throw it on the earth.” So he threw it on the earth, and it became a serpent; and Moses began to flee from it.

1605.label: Exodus 4:4
1605.text: Jehovah now said to Moses: “Thrust your hand out and grab hold of it by the tail.” So he thrust his hand out and grabbed hold of it, and it became a rod in his palm.

1606.label: Exodus 4:5
1606.text: “In order that,” to quote him, “they may believe that Jehovah the God of their forefathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.”

1607.label: Exodus 4:6
1607.text: Then Jehovah said to him once more: “Stick your hand, please, into the upper fold of your garment.” So he stuck his hand into the upper fold of his garment. When he drew it out, why, here his hand was stricken with leprosy like snow!

1608.label: Exodus 4:7
1608.text: After that he said: “Return your hand into the upper fold of your garment.” So he returned his hand into the upper fold of his garment. When he drew it out of the upper fold of his garment, why, here it was restored like the rest of his flesh!

1609.label: Exodus 4:8
1609.text: “And it must occur that,” to quote him, “if they will not believe you and will not listen to the voice of the first sign, then they will certainly believe the voice of the later sign.

1610.label: Exodus 4:9
1610.text: Still, it must occur that, if they will not believe even these two signs and will not listen to your voice, then you will have to take some water from the Nile River and pour it out on the dry land; and the water that you will take from the Nile River will certainly become, yes, it will indeed become blood on the dry land.”

1611.label: Exodus 4:10
1611.text: Moses now said to Jehovah: “Excuse me, Jehovah, but I am not a fluent speaker, neither since yesterday nor since before that nor since your speaking to your servant, for I am slow of mouth and slow of tongue.”

1612.label: Exodus 4:11
1612.text: At that Jehovah said to him: “Who appointed a mouth for man or who appoints the speechless or the deaf or the clear-sighted or the blind? Is it not I, Jehovah?

1613.label: Exodus 4:12
1613.text: So now go, and I myself shall prove to be with your mouth and I will teach you what you ought to say.”

1614.label: Exodus 4:13
1614.text: But he said: “Excuse me, Jehovah, but send, please, by the hand of the one whom you are going to send.”

1615.label: Exodus 4:14
1615.text: Then Jehovah’s anger grew hot against Moses and he said: “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I do know that he can really speak. And, besides, here he is on his way out to meet you. When he does see you, he will certainly rejoice in his heart.

1616.label: Exodus 4:15
1616.text: And you must speak to him and put the words in his mouth; and I myself shall prove to be with your mouth and his mouth, and I will teach YOU men what YOU are to do.

1617.label: Exodus 4:16
1617.text: And he must speak for you to the people; and it must occur that he will serve as a mouth to you, and you will serve as God to him.

1618.label: Exodus 4:17
1618.text: And this rod you will take in your hand that you may perform the signs with it.”

1619.label: Exodus 4:18
1619.text: Accordingly Moses went and returned to Jethʹro his father-in-law and said to him: “I want to go, please, and return to my brothers who are in Egypt that I may see whether they are still alive.” So Jethʹro said to Moses: “Go in peace.”

1620.label: Exodus 4:19
1620.text: After that Jehovah said to Moses in Midʹi·an: “Go, return to Egypt, because all the men who were hunting for your soul are dead.”

1621.label: Exodus 4:20
1621.text: Then Moses took his wife and his sons and made them ride on an ass, and he proceeded to return to the land of Egypt. Moreover, Moses took the rod of the [true] God in his hand.

1622.label: Exodus 4:21
1622.text: And Jehovah went on to say to Moses: “After you have gone and returned to Egypt see that YOU men actually perform all the miracles that I have put in your hand before Pharʹaoh. As for me, I shall let his heart become obstinate; and he will not send the people away.

1623.label: Exodus 4:22
1623.text: And you must say to Pharʹaoh, ‘This is what Jehovah has said: “Israel is my son, my firstborn.

1624.label: Exodus 4:23
1624.text: And I say to you: Send my son away that he may serve me. But should you refuse to send him away, here I am killing your son, your firstborn.”’”

1625.label: Exodus 4:24
1625.text: Now it came about on the road at the lodging place that Jehovah got to meet him and kept looking for a way to put him to death.

1626.label: Exodus 4:25
1626.text: Finally Zip·poʹrah took a flint and cut off her son’s foreskin and caused it to touch his feet and said: “It is because you are a bridegroom of blood to me.”

1627.label: Exodus 4:26
1627.text: Consequently he let go of him. At that time she said: “A bridegroom of blood,” because of the circumcision.

1628.label: Exodus 4:27
1628.text: Then Jehovah said to Aaron: “Go to meet Moses into the wilderness.” With that he went and met him in the mountain of the [true] God and kissed him.

1629.label: Exodus 4:28
1629.text: And Moses proceeded to tell Aaron all the words of Jehovah, who had sent him, and all the signs that he had commanded him to do.

1630.label: Exodus 4:29
1630.text: After that Moses and Aaron went and gathered all the older men of the sons of Israel.

1631.label: Exodus 4:30
1631.text: Then Aaron spoke all the words that Jehovah had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs under the eyes of the people.

1632.label: Exodus 4:31
1632.text: At this the people believed. When they heard that Jehovah had turned his attention to the sons of Israel and that he had seen their affliction, then they bowed down and prostrated themselves.

1633.label: Exodus 5:1
1633.text: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in and proceeded to say to Pharʹaoh: “This is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said, ‘Send my people away that they may celebrate a festival to me in the wilderness.’”

1634.label: Exodus 5:2
1634.text: But Pharʹaoh said: “Who is Jehovah, so that I should obey his voice to send Israel away? I do not know Jehovah at all and, what is more, I am not going to send Israel away.”

1635.label: Exodus 5:3
1635.text: However, they went on to say: “The God of the Hebrews has come in touch with us. We want to go, please, a journey of three days into the wilderness and sacrifice to Jehovah our God; otherwise he may strike at us with pestilence or with sword.”

1636.label: Exodus 5:4
1636.text: At this the king of Egypt said to them: “Why is it, Moses and Aaron, that YOU cause the people to leave off from their works? Go bearing YOUR burdens!”

1637.label: Exodus 5:5
1637.text: And Pharʹaoh continued: “Look! The people of the land are now many, and YOU indeed make them desist from their bearing of burdens.”

1638.label: Exodus 5:6
1638.text: Immediately on that day Pharʹaoh commanded those who drove the people to work and their officers, saying:

1639.label: Exodus 5:7
1639.text: “YOU must not gather straw to give to the people to make bricks as formerly. Let them themselves go and gather straw for themselves.

1640.label: Exodus 5:8
1640.text: Moreover, the required amount of bricks that they were making formerly, YOU will further impose upon them. YOU must not make any reduction for them, because they are relaxing. That is why they are crying out, saying, ‘We want to go, we want to sacrifice to our God!’

1641.label: Exodus 5:9
1641.text: Let the service be heavy upon the men and let them work at it, and let them not pay attention to false words.”

1642.label: Exodus 5:10
1642.text: So those who drove the people to work and their officers went out and said to the people: “Here is what Pharʹaoh has said, ‘I am giving YOU no more straw.

1643.label: Exodus 5:11
1643.text: YOU yourselves go, get straw for yourselves wherever YOU may find it, because there is to be no reducing of YOUR services one bit.’”

1644.label: Exodus 5:12
1644.text: Consequently the people scattered about over all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.

1645.label: Exodus 5:13
1645.text: And those who drove them to work kept urging them, saying: “Finish YOUR works, each one his work, day for day, just as when straw was available.”

1646.label: Exodus 5:14
1646.text: Later on the officers of the sons of Israel, whom Pharʹaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, these saying: “Why is it YOU did not finish YOUR prescribed task in making bricks as formerly, both yesterday and today?”

1647.label: Exodus 5:15
1647.text: Consequently the officers of the sons of Israel went in and began to cry out to Pharʹaoh, saying: “Why do you deal this way with your servants?

1648.label: Exodus 5:16
1648.text: There is no straw given to your servants and yet they are saying to us, ‘Make bricks!’ and here your servants are beaten, whereas your own people are at fault.”

1649.label: Exodus 5:17
1649.text: But he said: “YOU are relaxing, YOU are relaxing! That is why YOU are saying, ‘We want to go, we want to sacrifice to Jehovah.’

1650.label: Exodus 5:18
1650.text: And now go, serve! Though no straw will be given to YOU, yet YOU are to give the fixed amount of bricks.”

1651.label: Exodus 5:19
1651.text: Then the officers of the sons of Israel saw themselves in an evil plight at the saying: “YOU must not deduct from YOUR bricks one bit of anyone’s daily rate.”

1652.label: Exodus 5:20
1652.text: After that they encountered Moses and Aaron, who were standing there to meet them as they came out from Pharʹaoh.

1653.label: Exodus 5:21
1653.text: At once they said to them: “May Jehovah look upon YOU and judge, since YOU have made us smell offensive before Pharʹaoh and before his servants so as to put a sword in their hand to kill us.”

1654.label: Exodus 5:22
1654.text: Then Moses turned to Jehovah and said: “Jehovah, why have you caused evil to this people? Why is it that you have sent me?

1655.label: Exodus 5:23
1655.text: For from the time that I went in before Pharʹaoh to speak in your name, he has done evil to this people, and you have by no means delivered your people.”

1656.label: Exodus 6:1
1656.text: So Jehovah said to Moses: “Now you will see what I shall do to Pharʹaoh, because on account of a strong hand he will send them away and on account of a strong hand he will drive them out of his land.”

1657.label: Exodus 6:2
1657.text: And God went on to speak to Moses and to say to him: “I am Jehovah.

1658.label: Exodus 6:3
1658.text: And I used to appear to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as God Almighty, but as respects my name Jehovah I did not make myself known to them.

1659.label: Exodus 6:4
1659.text: And I also established my covenant with them to give them the land of Caʹnaan, the land of their alien residences in which they resided as aliens.

1660.label: Exodus 6:5
1660.text: And I, even I, have heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I remember my covenant.

1661.label: Exodus 6:6
1661.text: “Therefore say to the sons of Israel, ‘I am Jehovah, and I shall certainly bring YOU out from under the burdens of the Egyptians and deliver YOU from their slavery, and I shall indeed reclaim YOU with an outstretched arm and with great judgments.

1662.label: Exodus 6:7
1662.text: And I shall certainly take YOU to me as a people, and I shall indeed prove to be God to YOU; and YOU will certainly know that I am Jehovah YOUR God who is bringing YOU out from under the burdens of Egypt.

1663.label: Exodus 6:8
1663.text: And I shall certainly bring YOU into the land that I raised my hand in oath to give to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; and I shall indeed give it to YOU as something to possess. I am Jehovah.’”

1664.label: Exodus 6:9
1664.text: Afterward Moses spoke to this effect to the sons of Israel, but they did not listen to Moses out of discouragement and for the hard slavery.

1665.label: Exodus 6:10
1665.text: Then Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying:

1666.label: Exodus 6:11
1666.text: “Go in, speak to Pharʹaoh, Egypt’s king, that he should send the sons of Israel away out of his land.”

1667.label: Exodus 6:12
1667.text: However, Moses spoke before Jehovah, saying: “Look! The sons of Israel have not listened to me; and how will Pharʹaoh ever listen to me, as I am uncircumcised in lips?”

1668.label: Exodus 6:13
1668.text: But Jehovah continued to speak to Moses and Aaron and to issue the command by them to the sons of Israel and to Pharʹaoh, Egypt’s king, in order to bring the sons of Israel out from the land of Egypt.

1669.label: Exodus 6:14
1669.text: These are the heads of the house of their fathers: The sons of Reuʹben, Israel’s firstborn, were Haʹnoch and Palʹlu, Hezʹron and Carʹmi. These are the families of Reuʹben.

1670.label: Exodus 6:15
1670.text: And the sons of Simʹe·on were Jem·uʹel and Jaʹmin and Oʹhad and Jaʹchin and Zoʹhar and Shaʹul the son of a Caʹnaan·ite woman. These are the families of Simʹe·on.

1671.label: Exodus 6:16
1671.text: And these are the names of the sons of Leʹvi, according to their family descents: Gerʹshon and Koʹhath and Me·rarʹi. And the years of Leʹvi’s life were a hundred and thirty-seven years.

1672.label: Exodus 6:17
1672.text: The sons of Gerʹshon were Libʹni and Shimʹe·i, according to their families.

1673.label: Exodus 6:18
1673.text: And the sons of Koʹhath were Amʹram and Izʹhar and Heʹbron and Uzʹzi·el. And the years of Koʹhath’s life were a hundred and thirty-three years.

1674.label: Exodus 6:19
1674.text: And the sons of Me·rarʹi were Mahʹli and Muʹshi. These were the families of the Levites, according to their family descents.

1675.label: Exodus 6:20
1675.text: Now Amʹram took Jochʹe·bed his father’s sister as his wife. Later she bore him Aaron and Moses. And the years of Amʹram’s life were a hundred and thirty-seven years.

1676.label: Exodus 6:21
1676.text: And the sons of Izʹhar were Koʹrah and Neʹpheg and Zichʹri.

1677.label: Exodus 6:22
1677.text: And the sons of Uzʹzi·el were Mishʹa·el and El·zaʹphan and Sithʹri.

1678.label: Exodus 6:23
1678.text: Now Aaron took E·liʹshe·ba, Am·minʹa·dab’s daughter, the sister of Nahʹshon, as his wife. Later she bore him Naʹdab and A·biʹhu, El·e·aʹzar and Ithʹa·mar.

1679.label: Exodus 6:24
1679.text: And the sons of Koʹrah were Asʹsir and El·kaʹnah and A·biʹa·saph. These were the families of the Koʹrah·ites.

1680.label: Exodus 6:25
1680.text: And El·e·aʹzar, Aaron’s son, took for himself one of the daughters of Puʹti·el as his wife. Later she bore him Phinʹe·has. These are the heads of the fathers of the Levites, according to their families.

1681.label: Exodus 6:26
1681.text: This is the Aaron and Moses to whom Jehovah said: “BRING the sons of Israel out from the land of Egypt according to their armies.”

1682.label: Exodus 6:27
1682.text: They were the ones speaking to Pharʹaoh, Egypt’s king, to bring the sons of Israel out from Egypt. This is the Moses and Aaron.

1683.label: Exodus 6:28
1683.text: And it came about on the day that Jehovah spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,

1684.label: Exodus 6:29
1684.text: that Jehovah went on to speak to Moses, saying: “I am Jehovah. Speak to Pharʹaoh king of Egypt everything I am speaking to you.”

1685.label: Exodus 6:30
1685.text: Then Moses said before Jehovah: “Look! I am uncircumcised in lips, so how will Pharʹaoh ever listen to me?”

1686.label: Exodus 7:1
1686.text: Consequently Jehovah said to Moses: “See, I have made you God to Pharʹaoh, and Aaron your own brother will become your prophet.

1687.label: Exodus 7:2
1687.text: You—you will speak all that I shall command you; and Aaron your brother will do the speaking to Pharʹaoh, and he must send the sons of Israel away from his land.

1688.label: Exodus 7:3
1688.text: As for me, I shall let Pharʹaoh’s heart become obstinate, and I shall certainly multiply my signs and my miracles in the land of Egypt.

1689.label: Exodus 7:4
1689.text: And Pharʹaoh will not listen to YOU men; and I shall have to lay my hand upon Egypt and bring my armies, my people, the sons of Israel, out from the land of Egypt with great judgments.

1690.label: Exodus 7:5
1690.text: And the Egyptians will certainly know that I am Jehovah when I stretch out my hand against Egypt, and I shall indeed bring the sons of Israel out from their midst.”

1691.label: Exodus 7:6
1691.text: And Moses and Aaron went ahead doing as Jehovah had commanded them. They did just so.

1692.label: Exodus 7:7
1692.text: And Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three years old at the time of their speaking to Pharʹaoh.

1693.label: Exodus 7:8
1693.text: Jehovah now said to Moses and Aaron:

1694.label: Exodus 7:9
1694.text: “In case that Pharʹaoh speaks to YOU, saying, ‘Produce a miracle for yourselves,’ then you must say to Aaron, ‘Take your rod and throw it down before Pharʹaoh.’ It will become a big snake.”

1695.label: Exodus 7:10
1695.text: So Moses and Aaron went on in to Pharʹaoh and did exactly as Jehovah had commanded. Accordingly Aaron threw his rod down before Pharʹaoh and his servants and it became a big snake.

1696.label: Exodus 7:11
1696.text: However, Pharʹaoh also called for the wise men and the sorcerers; and the magic-practicing priests of Egypt themselves also proceeded to do the same thing with their magic arts.

1697.label: Exodus 7:12
1697.text: So they threw down each one his rod, and they became big snakes; but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.

1698.label: Exodus 7:13
1698.text: Still, Pharʹaoh’s heart became obstinate, and he did not listen to them, just as Jehovah had spoken.

1699.label: Exodus 7:14
1699.text: Then Jehovah said to Moses: “Pharʹaoh’s heart is unresponsive. He has refused to send the people away.

1700.label: Exodus 7:15
1700.text: Go to Pharʹaoh in the morning. Look! He is going out to the water! And you must put yourself in position to meet him by the edge of the Nile River, and the rod that turned into a serpent you are to take in your hand.

1701.label: Exodus 7:16
1701.text: And you must say to him, ‘Jehovah the God of the Hebrews has sent me to you, saying: “Send my people away that they may serve me in the wilderness,” but here you have not obeyed until now.

1702.label: Exodus 7:17
1702.text: This is what Jehovah has said: “By this you will know that I am Jehovah. Here I am striking with the rod that is in my hand upon the water that is in the Nile River, and it will certainly turn into blood.

1703.label: Exodus 7:18
1703.text: And the fish that are in the Nile River will die, and the Nile River will actually stink, and the Egyptians will simply have no stomach for drinking water from the Nile River.”’”

1704.label: Exodus 7:19
1704.text: Subsequently Jehovah said to Moses: “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your rod and stretch your hand out over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their Nile canals and over their reedy pools and over all their impounded waters, that they may become blood.’ And there will certainly be blood in all the land of Egypt and in the wooden vessels and in the stone vessels.”

1705.label: Exodus 7:20
1705.text: Immediately Moses and Aaron did so, just as Jehovah had commanded, and he lifted up the rod and struck the water that was in the Nile River under the eyes of Pharʹaoh and his servants, and all the water that was in the Nile River was turned into blood.

1706.label: Exodus 7:21
1706.text: And the fish that were in the Nile River died, and the Nile River began to stink; and the Egyptians were unable to drink water from the Nile River; and the blood came to be in all the land of Egypt.

1707.label: Exodus 7:22
1707.text: Nevertheless, the magic-practicing priests of Egypt proceeded to do the same thing with their secret arts; so that Pharʹaoh’s heart continued to be obstinate, and he did not listen to them, just as Jehovah had spoken.

1708.label: Exodus 7:23
1708.text: Hence Pharʹaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his heart to have any regard for this either.

1709.label: Exodus 7:24
1709.text: And all the Egyptians went digging round about the Nile River for water to drink, because they were unable to drink any water of the Nile River.

1710.label: Exodus 7:25
1710.text: And seven days came to be fulfilled after Jehovah’s striking the Nile River.

1711.label: Exodus 8:1
1711.text: Then Jehovah said to Moses: “Go in to Pharʹaoh, and you must say to him, ‘This is what Jehovah has said: “Send my people away that they may serve me.

1712.label: Exodus 8:2
1712.text: And if you keep refusing to send them away, here I am plaguing all your territory with frogs.

1713.label: Exodus 8:3
1713.text: And the Nile River will fairly teem with frogs, and they will certainly come up and enter into your house and your inner bedroom and upon your couch and into the houses of your servants and on your people and into your ovens and into your kneading troughs.

1714.label: Exodus 8:4
1714.text: And on you and on your people and on all your servants the frogs will come up.”’”

1715.label: Exodus 8:5
1715.text: Later on Jehovah said to Moses: “Say to Aaron, ‘Stretch your hand with your rod out over the rivers, the Nile canals and the reedy pools and make the frogs come up over the land of Egypt.’”

1716.label: Exodus 8:6
1716.text: At that Aaron stretched his hand out over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs began to come up and to cover the land of Egypt.

1717.label: Exodus 8:7
1717.text: However, the magic-practicing priests did the same thing by their secret arts and made the frogs come up over the land of Egypt.

1718.label: Exodus 8:8
1718.text: In time Pharʹaoh called Moses and Aaron and said: “Entreat Jehovah that he may remove the frogs from me and my people, as I want to send the people away that they may sacrifice to Jehovah.”

1719.label: Exodus 8:9
1719.text: Then Moses said to Pharʹaoh: “You take the glory over me to say when I shall make entreaty for you and your servants and your people in order to cut the frogs off from you and your houses. Only in the Nile River will they be left.”

1720.label: Exodus 8:10
1720.text: To this he said: “Tomorrow.” So he said: “It will be according to your word, in order that you may know that there is no one else like Jehovah our God,

1721.label: Exodus 8:11
1721.text: in that the frogs will certainly turn away from you and your houses and your servants and your people. Only in the Nile River will they be left.”

1722.label: Exodus 8:12
1722.text: Accordingly Moses and Aaron went out from Pharʹaoh, and Moses cried out to Jehovah because of the frogs that He had put upon Pharʹaoh.

1723.label: Exodus 8:13
1723.text: Then Jehovah did according to Moses’ word, and the frogs began to die off from the houses, the courtyards and the fields.

1724.label: Exodus 8:14
1724.text: And they went piling them up, heaps upon heaps, and the land began to stink.

1725.label: Exodus 8:15
1725.text: When Pharʹaoh got to see that relief had taken place, he made his heart unresponsive; and he did not listen to them, just as Jehovah had spoken.

1726.label: Exodus 8:16
1726.text: Jehovah now said to Moses: “Say to Aaron, ‘Stretch your rod out and strike the dust of the earth, and it must become gnats in all the land of Egypt.’”

1727.label: Exodus 8:17
1727.text: And they proceeded to do this. So Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod and struck the dust of the earth, and the gnats came to be on man and beast. All the dust of the earth became gnats in all the land of Egypt.

1728.label: Exodus 8:18
1728.text: And the magic-practicing priests tried to do the same by their secret arts, in order to bring forth gnats, but they were unable. And the gnats came to be on man and beast.

1729.label: Exodus 8:19
1729.text: Hence the magic-practicing priests said to Pharʹaoh: “It is the finger of God!” But Pharʹaoh’s heart continued to be obstinate, and he did not listen to them, just as Jehovah had spoken.

1730.label: Exodus 8:20
1730.text: Then Jehovah said to Moses: “Get up early in the morning and take a position in front of Pharʹaoh. Look! He is coming out to the water! And you must say to him, ‘This is what Jehovah has said: “Send my people away that they may serve me.

1731.label: Exodus 8:21
1731.text: But if you are not sending my people away, here I am sending upon you and your servants and your people and into your houses the gadfly; and the houses of Egypt will simply be full of the gadfly, and also the ground upon which they are.

1732.label: Exodus 8:22
1732.text: And on that day I shall certainly make the land of Goʹshen upon which my people are standing distinct, that no gadfly may exist there; in order that you may know that I am Jehovah in the midst of the earth.

1733.label: Exodus 8:23
1733.text: And I shall indeed set a demarcation between my people and your people. Tomorrow this sign will take place.”’”

1734.label: Exodus 8:24
1734.text: And Jehovah proceeded to do so; and heavy swarms of gadflies began to invade the house of Pharʹaoh and the houses of his servants and all the land of Egypt. The land came to ruin as a result of the gadflies.

1735.label: Exodus 8:25
1735.text: Finally Pharʹaoh called Moses and Aaron and said: “Go, sacrifice to YOUR God in the land.”

1736.label: Exodus 8:26
1736.text: But Moses said: “It is not admissible to do so, because we would sacrifice to Jehovah our God a thing detestable to the Egyptians. Suppose we would sacrifice a thing detestable to the Egyptians before their eyes; would they not stone us?

1737.label: Exodus 8:27
1737.text: We shall go a journey of three days into the wilderness and we shall definitely sacrifice to Jehovah our God just as he has said to us.”

1738.label: Exodus 8:28
1738.text: Pharʹaoh now said: “I—I shall send YOU away, and YOU will indeed sacrifice to Jehovah YOUR God in the wilderness. Only do not make it quite so far away that YOU are going. Make entreaty in my behalf.”

1739.label: Exodus 8:29
1739.text: Then Moses said: “Here I am going forth from you, and I shall indeed make entreaty to Jehovah, and the gadflies will certainly turn away from Pharʹaoh, his servants and his people tomorrow. Only let not Pharʹaoh trifle again in not sending the people away to sacrifice to Jehovah.”

1740.label: Exodus 8:30
1740.text: After that Moses went out from Pharʹaoh and made entreaty to Jehovah.

1741.label: Exodus 8:31
1741.text: So Jehovah did according to Moses’ word, and the gadflies turned away from Pharʹaoh, his servants and his people. Not one was left.

1742.label: Exodus 8:32
1742.text: However, Pharʹaoh made his heart unresponsive this time also and did not send the people away.

1743.label: Exodus 9:1
1743.text: Consequently Jehovah said to Moses: “Go in to Pharʹaoh and you must state to him, ‘This is what Jehovah the God of the Hebrews has said: “Send my people away that they may serve me.

1744.label: Exodus 9:2
1744.text: But if you continue refusing to send them away and you are still keeping hold of them,

1745.label: Exodus 9:3
1745.text: look! Jehovah’s hand is coming upon your livestock that is in the field. On the horses, the asses, the camels, the herd and the flock there will be a very heavy pestilence.

1746.label: Exodus 9:4
1746.text: And Jehovah will certainly make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, and not a thing of all that belongs to the sons of Israel will die.”’”

1747.label: Exodus 9:5
1747.text: Moreover, Jehovah set an appointed time, saying: “Tomorrow Jehovah will do this thing in the land.”

1748.label: Exodus 9:6
1748.text: Accordingly Jehovah did this thing on the next day, and all sorts of livestock of Egypt began to die; but not one of the livestock of the sons of Israel died.

1749.label: Exodus 9:7
1749.text: Then Pharʹaoh sent, and, look! not so much as one of Israel’s livestock had died. Nevertheless, Pharʹaoh’s heart continued to be unresponsive, and he did not send the people away.

1750.label: Exodus 9:8
1750.text: After that Jehovah said to Moses and Aaron: “Take for yourselves both hands full of soot from a kiln, and Moses must toss it toward the heavens in Pharʹaoh’s sight.

1751.label: Exodus 9:9
1751.text: And it must become a powder upon all the land of Egypt, and it must become boils breaking out with blisters upon man and beast in all the land of Egypt.”

1752.label: Exodus 9:10
1752.text: So they took the soot of a kiln and stood before Pharʹaoh, and Moses tossed it toward the heavens, and it became boils with blisters, breaking out on man and beast.

1753.label: Exodus 9:11
1753.text: And the magic-practicing priests were unable to stand before Moses as a result of the boils, because the boils had developed on the magic-practicing priests and on all the Egyptians.

1754.label: Exodus 9:12
1754.text: But Jehovah let Pharʹaoh’s heart become obstinate, and he did not listen to them, just as Jehovah had stated to Moses.

1755.label: Exodus 9:13
1755.text: Then Jehovah said to Moses: “Get up early in the morning and take a position in front of Pharʹaoh, and you must say to him, ‘This is what Jehovah the God of the Hebrews has said: “Send my people away that they may serve me.

1756.label: Exodus 9:14
1756.text: For at this time I am sending all my blows against your heart and upon your servants and your people, to the end that you may know that there is none like me in all the earth.

1757.label: Exodus 9:15
1757.text: For by now I could have thrust my hand out that I might strike you and your people with pestilence and that you might be effaced from the earth.

1758.label: Exodus 9:16
1758.text: But, in fact, for this cause I have kept you in existence, for the sake of showing you my power and in order to have my name declared in all the earth.

1759.label: Exodus 9:17
1759.text: Are you still behaving haughtily against my people in not sending them away?

1760.label: Exodus 9:18
1760.text: Here I am causing it to rain down tomorrow about this time a very heavy hail, the like of which has never occurred in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.

1761.label: Exodus 9:19
1761.text: And now send, bring all your livestock and all that is yours in the field under shelter. As for any man and beast that will be found in the field and not gathered into the house, the hail will have to come down upon them, and they will have to die.”’”

1762.label: Exodus 9:20
1762.text: Anyone who feared Jehovah’s word among Pharʹaoh’s servants caused his own servants and his livestock to flee into the houses,

1763.label: Exodus 9:21
1763.text: but whoever did not set his heart to have any regard for Jehovah’s word left his servants and his livestock in the field.

1764.label: Exodus 9:22
1764.text: Jehovah now said to Moses: “Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, that hail may come on all the land of Egypt, upon man and beast and all vegetation of the field in the land of Egypt.”

1765.label: Exodus 9:23
1765.text: So Moses stretched out his rod toward the heavens; and Jehovah gave thunders and hail, and fire would run down to the earth, and Jehovah kept making it rain down hail upon the land of Egypt.

1766.label: Exodus 9:24
1766.text: Thus there came hail, and fire quivering in among the hail. It was very heavy, so that there had not occurred any like it in all the land of Egypt from the time it became a nation.

1767.label: Exodus 9:25
1767.text: And the hail went striking at all the land of Egypt. The hail struck everything that was in the field, from man to beast, and all sorts of vegetation of the field; and it shattered all sorts of trees of the field.

1768.label: Exodus 9:26
1768.text: Only in the land of Goʹshen, where the sons of Israel were, there occurred no hail.

1769.label: Exodus 9:27
1769.text: Eventually Pharʹaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron and said to them: “I have sinned this time. Jehovah is righteous, and I and my people are in the wrong.

1770.label: Exodus 9:28
1770.text: Entreat Jehovah that this may be enough of the occurring of God’s thunders and hail. Then I am willing to send YOU away, and YOU will not stay any longer.”

1771.label: Exodus 9:29
1771.text: So Moses said to him: “As soon as I go out of the city I shall spread my hands up to Jehovah. The thunders will stop and the hail will not continue any longer, in order that you may know that the earth belongs to Jehovah.

1772.label: Exodus 9:30
1772.text: As for you and your servants, I know already that YOU will not even then show fear because of Jehovah God.”

1773.label: Exodus 9:31
1773.text: As it was, the flax and the barley had been struck, because the barley was in the ear and the flax had flower buds.

1774.label: Exodus 9:32
1774.text: But the wheat and the spelt had not been struck, because they were seasonally late.

1775.label: Exodus 9:33
1775.text: Moses now went out of the city from Pharʹaoh and spread his hands up to Jehovah, and the thunders and the hail began to stop and rain did not pour down on the earth.

1776.label: Exodus 9:34
1776.text: When Pharʹaoh got to see that the rain and the hail and the thunders had stopped, he went sinning again and making his heart unresponsive, he as well as his servants.

1777.label: Exodus 9:35
1777.text: And Pharʹaoh’s heart continued obstinate, and he did not send the sons of Israel away, just as Jehovah had stated by means of Moses.

1778.label: Exodus 10:1
1778.text: Then Jehovah said to Moses: “Go in to Pharʹaoh, because I—I have let his heart and the hearts of his servants become unresponsive, in order that I may set these signs of mine right before him,

1779.label: Exodus 10:2
1779.text: and in order that you may declare in the ears of your son and your son’s son how severely I have dealt with Egypt and my signs that I have established among them; and YOU will certainly know that I am Jehovah.”

1780.label: Exodus 10:3
1780.text: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharʹaoh and said to him: “This is what Jehovah the God of the Hebrews has said, ‘How long must you refuse to submit yourself to me? Send my people away that they may serve me.

1781.label: Exodus 10:4
1781.text: For if you continue refusing to send my people away, here I am bringing locusts within your boundaries tomorrow.

1782.label: Exodus 10:5
1782.text: And they will actually cover the visible surface of the earth and it will not be possible to see the earth; and they will simply eat up the rest of what has escaped, what has been left to YOU people by the hail, and they will certainly eat every sprouting tree of YOURS out of the field.

1783.label: Exodus 10:6
1783.text: And your houses and the houses of all your servants and the houses of all Egypt will be filled to an extent that your fathers and your fathers’ fathers have not seen it from the day of their existing upon the ground until this day.’” With that he turned and went out from Pharʹaoh.

1784.label: Exodus 10:7
1784.text: After that Pharʹaoh’s servants said to him: “How long will this man prove to be as a snare to us? Send the men away that they may serve Jehovah their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt has perished?”

1785.label: Exodus 10:8
1785.text: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharʹaoh, and he said to them: “Go, serve Jehovah YOUR God. Who in particular are the ones going?”

1786.label: Exodus 10:9
1786.text: Then Moses said: “With our young people and our old people we shall go. With our sons and our daughters, with our sheep and our cattle we shall go, for we have a festival to Jehovah.”

1787.label: Exodus 10:10
1787.text: In turn he said to them: “Let it prove to be so, that Jehovah is with YOU when I shall send YOU and YOUR little ones away! See, on the contrary, something evil is YOUR aim.

1788.label: Exodus 10:11
1788.text: Not so! Go, please, YOU who are able-bodied men, and serve Jehovah, because that is what YOU are seeking to secure.” With that they were driven out from before Pharʹaoh.

1789.label: Exodus 10:12
1789.text: Jehovah now said to Moses: “Stretch your hand out over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up over the land of Egypt and eat up all the vegetation of the land, everything that the hail has let remain.”

1790.label: Exodus 10:13
1790.text: At once Moses stretched his rod out over the land of Egypt, and Jehovah caused an east wind to blow upon the land all that day and all night. The morning came and the east wind carried the locusts.

1791.label: Exodus 10:14
1791.text: And the locusts began to come up over all the land of Egypt and to settle down upon all the territory of Egypt. They were very burdensome. Before them there had never turned up in this way locusts like them, and there will never turn up any in this way after them.

1792.label: Exodus 10:15
1792.text: And they went covering the visible surface of the entire land, and the land grew dark; and they went on eating up all the vegetation of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left; and there was left nothing green on the trees or on the vegetation of the field in all the land of Egypt.

1793.label: Exodus 10:16
1793.text: So Pharʹaoh hurriedly called Moses and Aaron and said: “I have sinned against Jehovah YOUR God and against YOU.

1794.label: Exodus 10:17
1794.text: And now pardon, please, my sin just this once and ENTREAT Jehovah YOUR God that he may turn away just this deadly plague from upon me.”

1795.label: Exodus 10:18
1795.text: So he went out from Pharʹaoh and made entreaty to Jehovah.

1796.label: Exodus 10:19
1796.text: Then Jehovah made a shift to a very stiff west wind, and it carried the locusts away and drove them into the Red Sea. Not a single locust was let remain in all the territory of Egypt.

1797.label: Exodus 10:20
1797.text: However, Jehovah let Pharʹaoh’s heart become obstinate, and he did not send the sons of Israel away.

1798.label: Exodus 10:21
1798.text: Jehovah then said to Moses: “Stretch your hand out toward the heavens, that darkness may occur over the land of Egypt and the darkness may be felt.”

1799.label: Exodus 10:22
1799.text: Moses immediately stretched his hand out toward the heavens, and a gloomy darkness began to occur in all the land of Egypt for three days.

1800.label: Exodus 10:23
1800.text: They did not see one another, and none of them got up from his own place three days; but for all the sons of Israel there proved to be light in their dwellings.

1801.label: Exodus 10:24
1801.text: After that Pharʹaoh called Moses and said: “Go, SERVE Jehovah. Only YOUR sheep and YOUR cattle will be detained. YOUR little ones also may go with YOU.”

1802.label: Exodus 10:25
1802.text: But Moses said: “You yourself will also give into our hands sacrifices and burnt offerings, as we must render them to Jehovah our God.

1803.label: Exodus 10:26
1803.text: And our livestock will also go with us. Not a hoof will be allowed to remain, because it is from them that we shall take some to worship Jehovah our God, and we ourselves do not know what we shall render in worship to Jehovah until our arriving there.”

1804.label: Exodus 10:27
1804.text: At this Jehovah let Pharʹaoh’s heart become obstinate, and he did not consent to send them away.

1805.label: Exodus 10:28
1805.text: So Pharʹaoh said to him: “Get out from me! Watch yourself! Do not try to see my face again, because on the day of your seeing my face you will die.”

1806.label: Exodus 10:29
1806.text: To this Moses said: “That is the way you have spoken. I shall not try to see your face anymore.”

1807.label: Exodus 11:1
1807.text: And Jehovah proceeded to say to Moses: “One plague more I am going to bring upon Pharʹaoh and Egypt. After that he will send YOU away from here. At the time he sends YOU away altogether, he will literally drive YOU out from here.

1808.label: Exodus 11:2
1808.text: Speak, now, in the ears of the people, that they should ask every man of his companion and every woman of her companion articles of silver and articles of gold.”

1809.label: Exodus 11:3
1809.text: Accordingly Jehovah gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians. The man Moses too was very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of Pharʹaoh’s servants and in the eyes of the people.

1810.label: Exodus 11:4
1810.text: And Moses went on to say: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘About midnight I am going out into the midst of Egypt,

1811.label: Exodus 11:5
1811.text: and every firstborn in the land of Egypt must die, from the firstborn of Pharʹaoh who is sitting on his throne to the firstborn of the maidservant who is at the hand mill and every firstborn of beast.

1812.label: Exodus 11:6
1812.text: And there will certainly occur a great outcry in all the land of Egypt, the like of which has never yet occurred, and the like of which will never be brought about again.

1813.label: Exodus 11:7
1813.text: But against any of the sons of Israel will no dog move eagerly its tongue, from man to beast; in order that YOU people may know that Jehovah can make a distinction between the Egyptians and the sons of Israel.’

1814.label: Exodus 11:8
1814.text: And all these servants of yours will certainly come down to me and prostrate themselves to me, saying, ‘Go, you and all the people who follow your steps.’ And after that I shall go out.” With that he went out from Pharʹaoh in the heat of anger.

1815.label: Exodus 11:9
1815.text: Then Jehovah said to Moses: “Pharʹaoh will not listen to YOU men, in order for my miracles to be increased in the land of Egypt.”

1816.label: Exodus 11:10
1816.text: And Moses and Aaron performed all these miracles before Pharʹaoh; but Jehovah would let Pharʹaoh’s heart become obstinate, so that he did not send the sons of Israel away from his land.

1817.label: Exodus 12:1
1817.text: Jehovah now said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt:

1818.label: Exodus 12:2
1818.text: “This month will be the start of the months for YOU. It will be the first of the months of the year for YOU.

1819.label: Exodus 12:3
1819.text: Speak to the entire assembly of Israel, saying, ‘On the tenth day of this month they are to take for themselves each one a sheep for the ancestral house, a sheep to a house.

1820.label: Exodus 12:4
1820.text: But if the household proves to be too small for the sheep, then he and his neighbor close by must take it into his house according to the number of souls; YOU should compute each one proportionate to his eating as regards the sheep.

1821.label: Exodus 12:5
1821.text: The sheep should prove to be sound, a male, a year old, for YOU. YOU may pick from the young rams or from the goats.

1822.label: Exodus 12:6
1822.text: And it must continue under safeguard by YOU until the fourteenth day of this month, and the whole congregation of the assembly of Israel must slaughter it between the two evenings.

1823.label: Exodus 12:7
1823.text: And they must take some of the blood and splash it upon the two doorposts and the upper part of the doorway belonging to the houses in which they will eat it.

1824.label: Exodus 12:8
1824.text: “‘And they must eat the flesh on this night. They should eat it roasted with fire and with unfermented cakes along with bitter greens.

1825.label: Exodus 12:9
1825.text: Do not eat any of it raw or boiled, cooked in water, but roast with fire, its head together with its shanks and its interior parts.

1826.label: Exodus 12:10
1826.text: And YOU must not leave any of it over till morning, but what is left over of it till morning YOU should burn with fire.

1827.label: Exodus 12:11
1827.text: And in this way YOU should eat it, with YOUR hips girded, sandals on YOUR feet and YOUR staff in YOUR hand; and YOU must eat it in haste. It is Jehovah’s passover.

1828.label: Exodus 12:12
1828.text: And I must pass through the land of Egypt on this night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast; and on all the gods of Egypt I shall execute judgments. I am Jehovah.

1829.label: Exodus 12:13
1829.text: And the blood must serve as YOUR sign upon the houses where YOU are; and I must see the blood and pass over YOU, and the plague will not come on YOU as a ruination when I strike at the land of Egypt.

1830.label: Exodus 12:14
1830.text: “‘And this day must serve as a memorial for YOU, and YOU must celebrate it as a festival to Jehovah throughout YOUR generations. As a statute to time indefinite YOU should celebrate it.

1831.label: Exodus 12:15
1831.text: Seven days YOU are to eat unfermented cakes. Yes, on the first day YOU are to take away sourdough from YOUR houses, because anyone eating what is leavened, from the first day down to the seventh, that soul must be cut off from Israel.

1832.label: Exodus 12:16
1832.text: And on the first day there is to take place for YOU a holy convention, and on the seventh day a holy convention. No work is to be done on them. Only what every soul needs to eat, that alone may be done for YOU.

1833.label: Exodus 12:17
1833.text: “‘And YOU must keep the festival of unfermented cakes, because on this very day I must bring YOUR armies out from the land of Egypt. And YOU must keep this day throughout YOUR generations as a statute to time indefinite.

1834.label: Exodus 12:18
1834.text: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening YOU are to eat unfermented cakes down till the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.

1835.label: Exodus 12:19
1835.text: Seven days no sourdough is to be found in YOUR houses, because anyone tasting what is leavened, whether he is an alien resident or a native of the land, that soul must be cut off from the assembly of Israel.

1836.label: Exodus 12:20
1836.text: Nothing leavened are YOU to eat. In all YOUR dwellings YOU are to eat unfermented cakes.’”

1837.label: Exodus 12:21
1837.text: Promptly Moses called all the older men of Israel and said to them: “Draw out and take for yourselves small cattle according to YOUR families, and slaughter the passover victim.

1838.label: Exodus 12:22
1838.text: And YOU must take a bunch of hyssop and dip it into the blood in a basin and strike upon the upper part of the doorway and upon the two doorposts some of the blood that is in the basin; and none of YOU should go out of the entrance of his house until morning.

1839.label: Exodus 12:23
1839.text: Then when Jehovah does pass through to plague the Egyptians and does see the blood upon the upper part of the doorway and upon the two doorposts, Jehovah will certainly pass over the entrance, and he will not allow the ruination to enter into YOUR houses to plague YOU.

1840.label: Exodus 12:24
1840.text: “And YOU must keep this thing as a regulation for you and your sons to time indefinite.

1841.label: Exodus 12:25
1841.text: And it must occur that when YOU come into the land that Jehovah will give YOU, just as he has stated, then YOU must keep this service.

1842.label: Exodus 12:26
1842.text: And it must occur that when YOUR sons say to YOU, ‘What does this service mean to YOU?’

1843.label: Exodus 12:27
1843.text: then YOU must say, ‘It is the sacrifice of the passover to Jehovah, who passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when he plagued the Egyptians, but he delivered our houses.’” Then the people bowed low and prostrated themselves.

1844.label: Exodus 12:28
1844.text: Subsequently the sons of Israel went and did just as Jehovah had commanded Moses and Aaron. They did just so.

1845.label: Exodus 12:29
1845.text: And it came about that at midnight Jehovah struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharʹaoh sitting on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the prison hole, and every firstborn of beast.

1846.label: Exodus 12:30
1846.text: Then Pharʹaoh got up at night, he and all his servants and all [other] Egyptians; and there began arising a great outcry among the Egyptians, because there was not a house where there was not one dead.

1847.label: Exodus 12:31
1847.text: At once he called Moses and Aaron by night and said: “Get up, get out from the midst of my people, both YOU and the [other] sons of Israel, and go, serve Jehovah, just as YOU have stated.

1848.label: Exodus 12:32
1848.text: Take both YOUR flocks and YOUR herds, just as YOU have stated, and go. Also, YOU must bless me besides.”

1849.label: Exodus 12:33
1849.text: And the Egyptians began to urge the people in order to send them away quickly out of the land, “because,” they said, “we are all as good as dead!”

1850.label: Exodus 12:34
1850.text: Consequently the people carried their flour dough before it was leavened, with their kneading troughs wrapped up in their mantles upon their shoulder.

1851.label: Exodus 12:35
1851.text: And the sons of Israel did according to the word of Moses in that they went asking from the Egyptians articles of silver and articles of gold and mantles.

1852.label: Exodus 12:36
1852.text: And Jehovah gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, so that these granted them what was asked; and they stripped the Egyptians.

1853.label: Exodus 12:37
1853.text: And the sons of Israel proceeded to depart from Ramʹe·ses for Sucʹcoth, to the number of six hundred thousand able-bodied men on foot, besides little ones.

1854.label: Exodus 12:38
1854.text: And a vast mixed company also went up with them, as well as flocks and herds, a very numerous stock of animals.

1855.label: Exodus 12:39
1855.text: And they began to bake the flour dough that they had brought out from Egypt into round cakes, unfermented cakes, because it had not leavened, for they had been driven out of Egypt and had not been able to linger and too they had not prepared any provisions for themselves.

1856.label: Exodus 12:40
1856.text: And the dwelling of the sons of Israel, who had dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.

1857.label: Exodus 12:41
1857.text: And it came about at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, it even came about on this very day that all the armies of Jehovah went out of the land of Egypt.

1858.label: Exodus 12:42
1858.text: It is a night for observance with regard to Jehovah for bringing them out of the land of Egypt. With regard to Jehovah this night is one for observance on the part of all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.

1859.label: Exodus 12:43
1859.text: And Jehovah went on to say to Moses and Aaron: “This is the statute of the passover: No foreigner may eat of it.

1860.label: Exodus 12:44
1860.text: But where there is any slave man purchased with money, you must circumcise him. Then first he may share in eating it.

1861.label: Exodus 12:45
1861.text: A settler and a hired laborer may not eat of it.

1862.label: Exodus 12:46
1862.text: In one house it is to be eaten. You must not take any of the flesh out of the house to some place outside. And YOU must not break a bone in it.

1863.label: Exodus 12:47
1863.text: All the assembly of Israel are to celebrate it.

1864.label: Exodus 12:48
1864.text: And in case an alien resident resides as an alien with you and he will actually celebrate the passover to Jehovah, let there be a circumcising of every male of his. First then he may come near to celebrate it; and he must become like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised man may eat of it.

1865.label: Exodus 12:49
1865.text: One law is to exist for the native and for the alien resident who is residing as an alien in YOUR midst.”

1866.label: Exodus 12:50
1866.text: So all the sons of Israel did just as Jehovah had commanded Moses and Aaron. They did just so.

1867.label: Exodus 12:51
1867.text: And it came about on this very day that Jehovah brought the sons of Israel together with their armies out of the land of Egypt.

1868.label: Exodus 13:1
1868.text: And Jehovah spoke further to Moses, saying:

1869.label: Exodus 13:2
1869.text: “Sanctify to me every male firstborn that opens each womb among the sons of Israel, among men and beasts. It is mine.”

1870.label: Exodus 13:3
1870.text: And Moses went on to say to the people: “Let there be a remembering of this day on which YOU went out of Egypt, from the house of slaves, because by strength of hand Jehovah brought YOU out from here. So nothing leavened may be eaten.

1871.label: Exodus 13:4
1871.text: Today YOU are going out in the month of Aʹbib.

1872.label: Exodus 13:5
1872.text: And it must occur that when Jehovah will have brought you into the land of the Caʹnaan·ites and the Hitʹtites and the Amʹor·ites and the Hiʹvites and the Jebʹu·sites, which he swore to your forefathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, then you must render this service in this month.

1873.label: Exodus 13:6
1873.text: Seven days you are to eat unfermented cakes, and on the seventh day is a festival to Jehovah.

1874.label: Exodus 13:7
1874.text: Unfermented cakes are to be eaten for the seven days; and nothing leavened is to be seen with you, and no sourdough is to be seen with you within all your boundaries.

1875.label: Exodus 13:8
1875.text: And you must tell your son on that day, saying, ‘It is because of that which Jehovah has done to me when I came out of Egypt.’

1876.label: Exodus 13:9
1876.text: And it must serve for you as a sign upon your hand and as a memorial between your eyes, in order that Jehovah’s law may prove to be in your mouth; because by a strong hand Jehovah brought you out of Egypt.

1877.label: Exodus 13:10
1877.text: And you must keep this statute at its appointed time from year to year.

1878.label: Exodus 13:11
1878.text: “And it must occur that when Jehovah brings you into the land of the Caʹnaan·ites, just as he has sworn to you and to your forefathers, and when he does give it to you,

1879.label: Exodus 13:12
1879.text: then you must devote everyone that opens the womb to Jehovah, and every firstling, the young of a beast, which will come to be yours. The males belong to Jehovah.

1880.label: Exodus 13:13
1880.text: And every firstling ass you are to redeem with a sheep, and if you will not redeem it, then you must break its neck. And every firstborn of man among your sons you are to redeem.

1881.label: Exodus 13:14
1881.text: “And it must occur that in case your son should inquire of you later on, saying, ‘What does this mean?’ then you must say to him, ‘By strength of hand Jehovah brought us out of Egypt, from the house of slaves.

1882.label: Exodus 13:15
1882.text: And it came about that Pharʹaoh showed obstinacy toward sending us away, and Jehovah proceeded to kill every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of man to the firstborn of beast. That is why I am sacrificing to Jehovah all the males that open the womb, and every firstborn of my sons I redeem.’

1883.label: Exodus 13:16
1883.text: And it must serve as a sign upon your hand and as a frontlet band between your eyes, because by strength of hand Jehovah brought us out of Egypt.”

1884.label: Exodus 13:17
1884.text: And it came about at the time of Pharʹaoh’s sending the people away that God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Phi·lisʹtines just because it was near, for God said: “It might be the people will feel regret when they see war and will certainly return to Egypt.”

1885.label: Exodus 13:18
1885.text: Hence God made the people go round about by the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea. But it was in battle formation that the sons of Israel went up out of the land of Egypt.

1886.label: Exodus 13:19
1886.text: And Moses was taking Joseph’s bones with him, because he had made the sons of Israel solemnly swear, saying: “God will without fail turn his attention to YOU, and YOU must take my bones up out of here with YOU.”

1887.label: Exodus 13:20
1887.text: And they proceeded to depart from Sucʹcoth and to encamp at Eʹtham at the edge of the wilderness.

1888.label: Exodus 13:21
1888.text: And Jehovah was going ahead of them in the daytime in a pillar of cloud to lead them by the way, and in the nighttime in a pillar of fire to give them light to go in the daytime and nighttime.

1889.label: Exodus 13:22
1889.text: The pillar of cloud would not move away from before the people in the daytime nor the pillar of fire in the nighttime.

1890.label: Exodus 14:1
1890.text: Jehovah now spoke to Moses, saying:

1891.label: Exodus 14:2
1891.text: “Speak to the sons of Israel, that they should turn back and encamp before Pi·ha·hiʹroth between Migʹdol and the sea in view of Baʹal-zeʹphon. In front of it YOU are to encamp by the sea.

1892.label: Exodus 14:3
1892.text: Then Pharʹaoh will certainly say respecting the sons of Israel, ‘They are wandering in confusion in the land. The wilderness has closed in upon them.’

1893.label: Exodus 14:4
1893.text: So I shall indeed let Pharʹaoh’s heart become obstinate, and he will certainly chase after them and I shall get glory for myself by means of Pharʹaoh and all his military forces; and the Egyptians will certainly know that I am Jehovah.” Accordingly they did just that.

1894.label: Exodus 14:5
1894.text: Later it was reported to the king of Egypt that the people had run away. Immediately the heart of Pharʹaoh as well as his servants was changed regarding the people, so that they said: “What is this that we have done, in that we have sent Israel away from slaving for us?”

1895.label: Exodus 14:6
1895.text: So he proceeded to make his war chariots ready, and he took his people with him.

1896.label: Exodus 14:7
1896.text: And he proceeded to take six hundred chosen chariots and all the other chariots of Egypt and warriors upon every one of them.

1897.label: Exodus 14:8
1897.text: Thus Jehovah let the heart of Pharʹaoh the king of Egypt become obstinate, and he went chasing after the sons of Israel, while the sons of Israel were going out with uplifted hand.

1898.label: Exodus 14:9
1898.text: And the Egyptians went chasing after them, and all the chariot horses of Pharʹaoh and his cavalrymen and his military forces were overtaking them while camping by the sea, by Pi·ha·hiʹroth in view of Baʹal-zeʹphon.

1899.label: Exodus 14:10
1899.text: When Pharʹaoh got close by, the sons of Israel began to raise their eyes and here the Egyptians were marching after them; and the sons of Israel got quite afraid and began to cry out to Jehovah.

1900.label: Exodus 14:11
1900.text: And they proceeded to say to Moses: “Is it because there are no burial places at all in Egypt that you have taken us here to die in the wilderness? What is this that you have done to us in leading us out of Egypt?

1901.label: Exodus 14:12
1901.text: Is this not the word we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than for us to die in the wilderness.”

1902.label: Exodus 14:13
1902.text: Then Moses said to the people: “Do not be afraid. Stand firm and see the salvation of Jehovah, which he will perform for YOU today. For the Egyptians whom YOU do see today YOU will not see again, no, never again.

1903.label: Exodus 14:14
1903.text: Jehovah will himself fight for YOU, and YOU yourselves will be silent.”

1904.label: Exodus 14:15
1904.text: Jehovah now said to Moses: “Why do you keep crying out to me? Speak to the sons of Israel that they should break camp.

1905.label: Exodus 14:16
1905.text: As for you, lift up your rod and stretch your hand out over the sea and split it apart, that the sons of Israel may go through the midst of the sea on dry land.

1906.label: Exodus 14:17
1906.text: As for me, here I am letting the hearts of the Egyptians become obstinate, that they may go in after them and that I may get glory for myself by means of Pharʹaoh and all his military forces, his war chariots and his cavalrymen.

1907.label: Exodus 14:18
1907.text: And the Egyptians will certainly know that I am Jehovah when I get glory for myself by means of Pharʹaoh, his war chariots and his cavalrymen.”

1908.label: Exodus 14:19
1908.text: Then the angel of the [true] God who was going ahead of the camp of Israel departed and went to their rear, and the pillar of cloud departed from their van and stood in the rear of them.

1909.label: Exodus 14:20
1909.text: So it came in between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel. On the one hand it proved to be a cloud together with darkness. On the other hand it kept lighting up the night. And this group did not come near that group all night long.

1910.label: Exodus 14:21
1910.text: Moses now stretched his hand out over the sea; and Jehovah began making the sea go back by a strong east wind all night long and converting the sea basin into dry ground, and the waters were being split apart.

1911.label: Exodus 14:22
1911.text: At length the sons of Israel went through the midst of the sea on dry land, while the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.

1912.label: Exodus 14:23
1912.text: And the Egyptians took up the pursuit, and all the horses of Pharʹaoh, his war chariots and his cavalrymen began going in after them, into the midst of the sea.

1913.label: Exodus 14:24
1913.text: And it came about during the morning watch that Jehovah began to look out upon the camp of the Egyptians from within the pillar of fire and cloud, and he went throwing the camp of the Egyptians into confusion.

1914.label: Exodus 14:25
1914.text: And he kept taking wheels off their chariots so that they were driving them with difficulty; and the Egyptians began to say: “Let us flee from any contact with Israel, because Jehovah certainly fights for them against the Egyptians.”

1915.label: Exodus 14:26
1915.text: Finally Jehovah said to Moses: “Stretch your hand out over the sea, that the waters may come back over the Egyptians, their war chariots and their cavalrymen.”

1916.label: Exodus 14:27
1916.text: Moses at once stretched his hand out over the sea, and the sea began to come back to its normal condition at the approaching of morning. All the while the Egyptians were fleeing from encountering it, but Jehovah shook the Egyptians off into the midst of the sea.

1917.label: Exodus 14:28
1917.text: And the waters kept coming back. Finally they covered the war chariots and the cavalrymen belonging to all of Pharʹaoh’s military forces and who had gone into the sea after them. Not so much as one among them was let remain.

1918.label: Exodus 14:29
1918.text: As for the sons of Israel, they walked on dry land in the midst of the seabed, and the waters were for them a wall on their right hand and on their left.

1919.label: Exodus 14:30
1919.text: Thus on that day Jehovah saved Israel from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel got to see the Egyptians dead on the seashore.

1920.label: Exodus 14:31
1920.text: Israel also got to see the great hand that Jehovah put in action against the Egyptians; and the people began to fear Jehovah and to put faith in Jehovah and in Moses his servant.

1921.label: Exodus 15:1
1921.text: At that time Moses and the sons of Israel proceeded to sing this song to Jehovah and to say the following: “Let me sing to Jehovah, for he has become highly exalted. The horse and its rider he has pitched into the sea.

1922.label: Exodus 15:2
1922.text: My strength and [my] might is Jah, since he serves for my salvation. This is my God, and I shall laud him; my father’s God, and I shall raise him on high.

1923.label: Exodus 15:3
1923.text: Jehovah is a manly person of war. Jehovah is his name.

1924.label: Exodus 15:4
1924.text: Pharʹaoh’s chariots and his military forces he has cast into the sea, And the choice of his warriors have been sunk in the Red Sea.

1925.label: Exodus 15:5
1925.text: The surging waters proceeded to cover them; down they went into the depths like a stone.

1926.label: Exodus 15:6
1926.text: Your right hand, O Jehovah, is proving itself powerful in ability, Your right hand, O Jehovah, can shatter an enemy.

1927.label: Exodus 15:7
1927.text: And in the abundance of your superiority you can throw down those who rise up against you; You send out your burning anger, it eats them up like stubble.

1928.label: Exodus 15:8
1928.text: And by a breath from your nostrils waters were heaped up;They stood still like a dam of floods;The surging waters were congealed in the heart of the sea.

1929.label: Exodus 15:9
1929.text: The enemy said, ‘I shall pursue! I shall overtake! I shall divide spoil! My soul will be filled with them!I shall draw my sword! My hand will drive them away!’

1930.label: Exodus 15:10
1930.text: You blew with your breath, the sea covered them; They sank like lead in majestic waters.

1931.label: Exodus 15:11
1931.text: Who among the gods is like you, O Jehovah? Who is like you, proving yourself mighty in holiness? The One to be feared with songs of praise, the One doing marvels.

1932.label: Exodus 15:12
1932.text: You stretched out your right hand, the earth proceeded to swallow them up.

1933.label: Exodus 15:13
1933.text: You in your loving-kindness have led the people whom you have recovered; You in your strength will certainly conduct them to your holy abiding place.

1934.label: Exodus 15:14
1934.text: Peoples must hear, they will be agitated; Birth pangs must take hold on the inhabitants of Phi·lisʹti·a.

1935.label: Exodus 15:15
1935.text: At that time the sheiks of Eʹdom will indeed be disturbed;As for the despots of Moʹab, trembling will take hold on them. All the inhabitants of Caʹnaan will indeed be disheartened.

1936.label: Exodus 15:16
1936.text: Fright and dread will fall upon them. Because of the greatness of your arm they will be motionless like a stone,Until your people pass by, O Jehovah,Until the people whom you have produced pass by.

1937.label: Exodus 15:17
1937.text: You will bring them and plant them in the mountain of your inheritance, An established place that you have made ready for you to inhabit, O Jehovah,A sanctuary, O Jehovah, that your hands have established.

1938.label: Exodus 15:18
1938.text: Jehovah will rule as king to time indefinite, even forever.

1939.label: Exodus 15:19
